title: Francis (2013–2025)
hookLine: a Jesuit from Buenos Aires takes the name of the poor man of Assisi
carry: a poor church for the poor

cards: White smoke, a wet evening, a square full of umbrellas. A man in plain white steps onto the balcony of St Peter's and, for a moment, just stands there. Then he says good evening, like a neighbor.
Before he gives the crowd his blessing, he asks them for something: to pray for him first, in silence. He bows his head, and the square, full of noise a moment ago, goes quiet.
His name was Jorge Mario Bergoglio, a Jesuit and the archbishop of Buenos Aires. The name he chose was Francis.

teach.b: Start with the name. A few days later he told journalists how it happened. As the votes added up, a cardinal friend beside him hugged him and said, don't forget the poor.

And the name came to him: Francis of Assisi, the man of poverty, the man of peace, who loved creation. You've met him on this path before: the merchant's son who gave everything away. Second, the line.

teach.h: A CHURCH POOR, AND FOR THE POOR.
teach.b: In that same talk he said how much he would like a Church that is poor, and for the poor. That became today's line. Third, the habits.

teach.h: A GUESTHOUSE, A PRISON, A PHONE CALL.
teach.b: He lived in a guesthouse instead of the papal apartment. On Holy Thursday he often went to a prison and washed the feet of prisoners, women and men, Catholics and others.
He kept phoning ordinary people who had written to him. Small things, done deliberately.
Fourth, the scripture under it all: Jesus's parable of the judgment, in the Douay-Rheims: "as long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me."
Francis pointed to that chapter of Matthew more than once.
He had critics too: some Catholics found his style loose or his words unclear, and argued with his decisions on marriage and the liturgy; others felt he hadn't gone far enough.
Both arguments ran through his years as pope. But the first evening already held the picture: a man who bowed before he blessed the crowd, and asked a Church to stay close to the poor.

how: Catholics pray for the pope by name in the Eucharistic Prayer at every Mass; parishes take up Francis's emphasis through food pantries, prison ministry and visits to the sick and lonely.

games.q: you've just been elected pope, and you step onto the balcony before a huge crowd. what's your first move?
o: ask the crowd to pray for you first, and bow.
games.why: he said good evening, asked them to pray for him in silence, and bowed his head before he blessed them.

practice: Think of one simple thing within reach, small and deliberate the way Francis's acts were: learning the name of the person who sells you coffee, calling someone who lives alone, giving to someone who asks and looking them in the eye.
Pick one, don't make it bigger than it is, and notice where you'd be tempted to skip it. If you pray, ask for the nerve; if not, just decide.

wordCard.voice: Francis. Jorge Mario Bergoglio, a Jesuit from Buenos Aires, who took the name of Francis of Assisi because a friend told him not to forget the poor.

carryVoice: Your line: a poor church for the poor. It began with a friend's whisper: don't forget the poor. See you tomorrow.
